doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: The Vegas casino's closure
summary: Rumor says the other casinos forced it to close because it drew away their crowds.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: what happened, the powers that be down there, the other casinos, the crowds would leave. So there was no action, you know, the slot machines and the gambling, it cut in on their action, so as a result I guess they somehow forced the closure.
Yeah. I remember seeing a documentary about Vegas and I think you’re correct, somehow that happened.

Uh huh. They claimed that it was fantastic, said they had the best music and the best everything, dancers, comedians, but they had everybody: Flip Wilson, John Kirby, they’d have all — I guess I don’t know about Richard Pryor, but they had all the best of everything, the best dancers and everything.
